clue.text: Moors see about a mongrel before Sabbath

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for see wraps the dog

parts.note: taken as written
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Moorland dwellers glimpse a stray dog just before the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to make it fast, so moors is a synonym of fastens in the nautical sense.

clue.text: Channel island without a note before morning as to mariners' guide

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the island's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France

indicators.note: before places the note and the a ahead of the morning abbreviation

parts.note: E is a musical note
M is short for morning, as in a.m.

explanation.surface: A sailor's directions about passing a Channel island early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark or beacon visible from the sea, used by sailors to fix their position.

clue.text: Shift

parts.note: a shift is both a change and a loose dress, so one word hints at swapping one's garments

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is an old word for a chemise, and to shift once meant to change one's dress.

clue.text: Set drama

parts.note: a set here is a wireless receiver, so this is a play broadcast to be heard on one

explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set receives broadcast plays, so drama for the set is a broadcast play for listeners.

clue.text: Healthy noise

definitions.meaning: healthy as in in good condition

explanation.definitionFit: Sound means in good condition, as in safe and sound, and is also any audible noise.

clue.text: Where vegetables are found panicking?

definitions.meaning: vegetables simmered in a pot of meat and broth
flustered and anxious, an idiom for agitation

explanation.definitionFit: A stew contains vegetables, and the idiom for being agitated or flustered is the same phrase.

clue.text: Incomers run and stride all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Newcomers race and stride about in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Intruders are people who come in uninvited, a sharper sense of incomers.

clue.text: National in Berkshire

parts.note: the Grand National is a famous horse race, so a racing venue found in the county of Berkshire

explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the celebrated racecourse in Berkshire, an English county west of London, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: These give the lie to experience in yarn-spinning

definitions.text: These give the lie to experience in yarn-spinning

parts.words: These give the lie to experience in yarn-spinning
parts.note: exaggerated stories told by those back from journeys, fibs about what they have seen

explanation.definitionFit: Tall stories told by people returning from abroad are proverbially embellished fibs.

clue.text: Ceases to be indifferent, festivities being at an end?

parts.note: wakes are local annual holidays and festivities in northern England
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: Someone stirs from apathy just as the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse oneself from apathy is to become alert, an idiomatic sense of starting to care.

clue.text: Some poser: animal, vegetable, mineral and abstract

definitions.text: Some poser: animal, vegetable, mineral and abstract

parts.words: Some poser: animal, vegetable, mineral and abstract
parts.note: the parlour guessing game asks animal, vegetable or mineral, and a nut can be a vegetable, hard a mineral quality, a crack an abstract break

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a difficult problem or person, so a real poser of a question.

clue.text: A long sort of national epithet

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters of long are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather lengthy description of a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix used to describe English nationality, as in Anglo-French, works as an epithet for a nation.

clue.text: Make us ten lads brave

indicators.note: make in the sense of form into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An order to train ten young men into courageous fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and undaunted, so a straightforward synonym for courageous.

clue.text: Kew longed possibly for learning

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters in Kew longed

explanation.surface: The botanic gardens at Kew yearned for scholarship, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning as a noun means acquired knowledge or scholarship, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sacks

parts.note: sacks as a verb, to fire someone from a job

explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to fire them from employment, so sacks is a synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Dance music

definitions.meaning: a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in two-four time
a piece of music written for that dance

explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a brisk dance and also the name for music composed for it.

clue.text: It is bursting to make its mark all around

definitions.text: It is bursting to make its mark all around

parts.words: It is bursting to make its mark all around
parts.note: an ambitious person seems described, but it is a cannon load of small balls that scatters on firing

explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon, spreading over a wide area.

clue.text: Shaky boy

definitions.meaning: unsound or weak, as in a dodgy heart
a pet form of Richard, a boy's name

explanation.definitionFit: Dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable, and is also a familiar form of Richard.

clue.text: Richard, look — an artist

parts.note: Dick is a familiar form of Richard
see means look

explanation.surface: Someone tells Richard to look at a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Frank Dicksee was a Victorian painter, so this is a specific example of an artist.

clue.text: Ass twice far removed from this tree

indicators.note: read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are rearranged
twice means the word for donkey appears two times

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A donkey, twice over, a long way from a particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassafras is a North American tree of the laurel family, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Remains later than intended, suitably corseted

definitions.meaning: with the stays, a corset's stiffening, kept on the body

explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to remain beyond the planned time, and stays are a corset, worn on.

clue.text: One-way roundabout

parts.note: a road junction is suggested, but it describes turning in a single fixed direction like a watch's hands

explanation.definitionFit: Clockwise means turning round in the same direction as a clock's hands, so one way round.

clue.text: Recognised in the bank now naturally

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words bank now naturally

explanation.surface: The riverbank is acknowledged now, as one would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recognised is acknowledged or familiar, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Puckish fine arranged — about a pound

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reworked letters surround the pound sign
arranged means the letters of fine are put in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A mischievous fine has been set at roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EFIN (the anagram of FINE from 'arranged') around L. Puck is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Puckish means mischievous like a sprite, and elfin means small and fairy-like.

clue.text: Casual performer in the next race

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies within the words next race

explanation.surface: A part-time actor runs in the following heat.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a non-speaking performer hired casually for crowd scenes in a film.

clue.text: Centres of 12 across for spouters?

parts.note: places of learning for creatures that spout water, read literally; spouters also suggests windbags

explanation.definitionFit: A school is a group of whales, so the playful idea of colleges for whales gives the phrase.

clue.text: Garbled, meaningless directions for ancient Jewish ascetics

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so the run of compass points is mixed up

parts.note: a pointless string of compass points such as south, east, north

explanation.surface: Confused, pointless instructions for old religious hermits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were a Jewish sect of ascetics at the time of the Second Temple, an example of ascetics.

clue.text: Different from the case of being completely virtuous in other words

definitions.meaning: free from any wrongdoing at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'in other words' tells you to re-space the letters: read as NOT AS IN they mean unlike, and as NOT A SIN they mean blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced one way the letters mean unlike, the other way they describe a blameless act.
